story.head: Expect a grind
paras: The Flyers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Vancouver on Nov 9. The Flyers have won two in a row, while the Canucks (5-18-1) lost 5-1 to Seattle on Nov 19. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Flyers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 20th in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.229) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .323, mostly because they’re 3-5 in one-goal games. The Flyers’ record (.440) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.38 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Flyers take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). Philadelphia has scored 2.52 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one. On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Brock Boeser (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 24 GP) leads the Canucks in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Elias Pettersson (#40) (6 G / 17 A / 23 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Flyers, Matvei Michkov (11 G / 8 A / 19 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.

Leevi Meriläinen (3-10-1 / .889 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for Vancouver. Philadelphia has two options in net: Joseph Woll (5-6-2 / .892 SV% in 13 GS) and Dan Vladař (3-5-4 / .874 SV% in 12 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Woll got the last one on Nov 19. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
